name: Colorado
nameStory: Spanish for 'colored red,' named for the Colorado River running rusty with canyon silt. The state is named after the color of its own mud.
capitalStory: Denver is the Mile High City: the thirteenth step of the State Capitol sits at exactly 5,280 feet. The town was named to flatter territorial governor James Denver, except the flattery arrived late - he had already resigned, and never came.

majorFeatures.name: Great Sand Dunes
majorFeatures.note: Tallest dunes in North America, 750 ft

funFacts: Admitted in 1876, exactly 100 years after the Declaration of Independence - hence 'Centennial State.'
It has the highest average elevation of any state, and no point in it is below 3,300 feet.
It looks like a perfect rectangle but isn't: 19th-century survey errors left the border with roughly 697 sides.
Colorado has more 14,000-foot peaks than the other 49 states combined.
whyItMatters: Snow that falls in the Colorado Rockies becomes drinking water for about 40 million people across seven states and Mexico. When the snowpack is thin here, cities a thousand miles away ration.
